headline: Revised institutional zone ordinance for University of New England land adds rules for minor structures on conservation land.
summary: The parcel, labeled IN 1B, is more than 300 acres, and three conservation easements cover part of it. The university asked for language allowing minor structures in the conservation areas, such as small footbridges and water bars, and the committee voted to add the easements' restrictions to RD6. Members also kept the map's 35-foot height limit and 30% lot coverage for the developable area. Staff is aiming for the planning board on November 18, then City Council for two readings, with the rules taking effect sometime in January.
decisions: Approved adding the conservation easement restrictions on structures to the RD6 rules.
Approved the institutional zone map, keeping the 35-foot height limit and 30% lot coverage for the developable area.
discussion: Conservation easement language: Members debated whether to copy the easement text into the ordinance or reference the deeds, and raised concern that the city does not enforce covenants. The university's representative said the easements allow minor structures such as footbridges and water bars, but not buildings.

Lot coverage on the map: Members questioned the 30% figure, which some recalled as 10%, and raised concern about wells and runoff on Newtown Road and Pool Street. No record of an earlier vote on 30% was found, so the map was kept as shown.
Buffer distance: Staff will remove the city's 30-foot buffer reference for university uses, so the new ordinance's 50-foot buffer applies. A 100-foot buffer was also suggested.
Future conservation rules: Members asked whether more land could join the conservation areas. A citywide overlay for sensitive areas, such as vernal pools, is expected sometime next year.
